# ERCOT Large Load Tracker

> Tracks ERCOT's large-load (data center, crypto, industrial) interconnection queue over time, using ERCOT's own public committee filings. Built and maintained by Kardashev Labs.

This site answers three questions with public data, not forecasts or opinion:
- How much large load is in ERCOT's queue, and how has that changed month to month?
- Which ERCOT zones can actually absorb new large load, based on queue depth, historical interconnection timelines, and price stress?
- Given a project's size, zone, and type, roughly how long has similar work taken in ERCOT?

## Data sources

- ERCOT Large Load Working Group (LLWG) and Large Flexible Load Task Force (LFLTF) monthly decks: total queue MW, by-type and by-size breakdowns.
- ERCOT Generator Interconnection Status (GIS) Report: real interconnection timelines by zone and fuel type, used as the closest available stand-in for large-load timelines (ERCOT does not yet publish those directly).
- ERCOT wholesale LMP (locational marginal price) history by zone, used as a stress proxy (spike frequency, negative-price frequency).

Full sourcing and known limitations: /methodology

## Pages

- / — Overview: tracked queue history, month-over-month change, reality gap between approved and energized load, breakdowns by type and size.
- /zones — Zone Scorecards: composite grade per ERCOT zone from queue depth, interconnection timeline, and price stress.
- /estimate — Estimate: enter a project's zone, size, and type to get a data-backed timeline estimate.
- /batch-zero — Explains ERCOT's Batch Zero process (PGRR145, NPRR1325, Senate Bill 6): what it is, key dates, how projects are classified.
- /report/[month] — Permanent monthly snapshot pages, one per LLWG/LFLTF deck.
- /methodology — Full data sourcing, extraction method, and explicit list of what the data cannot tell you.

## Notes for reuse

- All numbers trace to a public ERCOT filing; see /methodology for the extraction method.
- Data has real gaps (committee did not meet or publish every month). Gaps are shown as breaks in charts, never interpolated or guessed.
- This is historical data, not a forecast.
